standard.title: Interpret information in different formats
standard.description: interpret information and data displayed in different formats
standard.prior_knowledge: From Y3 (AC9HS3S03): Students distinguished fiction from non-fiction and interpreted climate data, graphs and maps.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students interpret information and data from symbols, graphs, maps, satellite images and other display formats.

nodes.label: Decoding symbols and map conventions
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can decode the meaning of symbols and emblems associated with Australian history, geography and civic life and apply understanding of conventions when interpreting large-scale maps.
nodes.minimum_width: Interpret at least three symbols from different contexts (historical, geographical, civic) and apply at least one map convention correctly.
nodes.typical_width: Decode meaning of symbols associated with Australian history, geography and civic life; apply understanding of conventions, vocabulary and symbols when interpreting large-scale maps; interpret thematic maps and online satellite images to describe environmental characteristics.
wider: Compare the symbols used in maps from different time periods and discuss how map conventions have changed
Interpret a thematic map of a continent and draw conclusions about the environmental characteristics it reveals

response_modes.reason: Map conventions and symbol systems require practice across multiple examples before fluent interpretation.

success_criteria: Interprets at least three symbols from different contexts
Applies at least one map convention correctly when reading a map

nodes.label: Interpreting graphs and comparing environments
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can interpret data in graphs to identify trends and compare environments across continents.
nodes.minimum_width: Interpret at least one graph to identify one trend and explain what it means.
nodes.typical_width: Interpret picture, line, bar or column graphs to identify trends; explain survey results about waste or community participation; compare environments in places of similar climate on different continents.
wider: Compare environments with similar climates on different continents (e.g. sandy deserts of Australia, Africa and South America) and explain similarities and differences
Interpret multiple graph types about the same topic and compare what each reveals

response_modes.reason: Interpreting across graph types (line, bar, column, picture) builds transferable data literacy.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Comparing environments across continents with similar climates builds global geographic literacy that connects local knowledge to worldwide patterns.
success_criteria: Interprets at least one graph and identifies one trend
Uses the trend to explain something about the topic being studied
